name: BrowserTabs
intent: Browser-style tab strip for switching between open documents or views, each with a close affordance.
when: Multi-document interfaces where each tab is a closeable open item

chooseOver.because: Tabs switch in-place content sections; BrowserTabs model openable/closeable documents like browser tabs
ViewTabBar is a lightweight underline view switcher; BrowserTabs are heavier document tabs

usage: Use BrowserTabs to help users navigate through your application or content hierarchy. This component provides clear wayfinding and helps users understand their current location within the interface.

BrowserTabs is ideal for multi-page applications, content-heavy interfaces, or any situation where users need to move between different sections. Keep navigation patterns consistent across your application for better user experience.

anatomy.description: BrowserTabs is composed of the following parts:

bestPractices.title: Keep tabs concise
bestPractices.description: Use short, descriptive labels for tab triggers.

bestPractices.title: Don't use long tab labels
bestPractices.description: Avoid lengthy text that causes tabs to wrap or overflow.

bestPractices.title: Maintain content relationship
bestPractices.description: Ensure tab content is clearly related to the tab label.

bestPractices.title: Don't use for navigation
bestPractices.description: Use proper navigation components for page-level routing.

bestPractices.title: Show active state clearly
bestPractices.description: Make the selected tab visually distinct from others.

bestPractices.title: Don't hide the active indicator
bestPractices.description: Always show which tab is currently selected.
